correctness.rationale: Exact multiplication gives three vertex types and complete directed arc list. The invariant decomposition yields q−1 nilpotent length-two Jordan chains, 2q(q−2) trivial zero chains, q−2 eigenvalue −1 chains, and the explicit 3-by-3 quotient with cubic P_q. The discriminant is nonzero for every prime power q≥2, so the cubic roots are simple. Direct exact reconstruction and characteristic/rank checks over q=2,3,4,5 succeeded. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the all-q proof.

originality.rationale: Three published-finding corpus semantic searches and targeted literature searches found no direct all-field complex Jordan/rank-stabilization statement. Li–Tucci 2013 supplies the *known directed graph*, not claimed as new. Sherin 2020 gives a different symmetric adjacency example, and Mönius 2020 treats finite commutative rings. The assessed finite-field all-parameter nilpotent Jordan decomposition and rank stabilization require additional spectral analysis. A complete Li–Tucci article was not accessible; its full graph description is an explicitly unresolved historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: The Li–Tucci 2013 paper explicitly says it fully describes the directed two-by-two graph; its inaccessible full text could make this Jordan theorem an unnoticed immediate corollary or contain equivalent formulas.
The 2020 paper treats a symmetric graph and its 5-vertex eigenvalues; the object distinction is clear from accessible text, but we did not independently obtain its complete PDF as a small file.
Semantic search and selected primary literature cannot establish global uniqueness; older adjacency-operator literature may contain an equivalent formula.

value.rationale: The complete complex Jordan type determines otherwise-hidden nilpotent walk propagation in a strongly connected directed ring graph: the adjacency rank is 2q on (2q+1)(q−1) vertices but all subsequent positive powers from the square onward have rank q+1. This natural infinite-family graph invariant is distinct from previously counted edges, girth/diameter and symmetric eigenvalues.
